findings.title: Batch tenant lookup always receives an empty ID list
findings.failure: recordsWithTenantStubs explicitly excludes records with nonempty tenantExternalIds. Flattening its external IDs therefore always produces []. HubSpot, Salesforce and Attio customers with account references consequently lose membership creation; tenant-centric imports skip those customers entirely and record successful skips.
findings.fix: Collect IDs from inRecords. Verify existing-account membership and tenant-centric import cases. If deployed, affected completed batches need a fresh import; rolling back code alone will not repair them.
findings.evidence: The filter at lines 485-487 guarantees an empty lookup input. Lines 327-350 interpret the empty map as nonexistent tenants. The three CRM toCustomer mappers populate tenantExternalIds. HEAD~1 performed the lookup per customer. handleImportSyncMessage.ts:551 records skipped progress as completed, and its batch-start guard skips terminal batches. The added importCustomers.tenants.litest.ts:164 test expects a lookup that this implementation cannot execute.

findings.title: Single-customer imports no longer resolve tenant references
findings.failure: When tenantsByExternalId is omitted, the implementation substitutes an empty map instead of querying tenants. Existing single-record callers therefore silently omit memberships for customers carrying tenantExternalIds. Correcting the batch ID selection does not fix these callers.
findings.fix: When the optional map is absent, resolve the record's tenantExternalIds through the aggregate and propagate lookup errors through scope.fail. Add coverage for importCustomer without a supplied map.
findings.evidence: HEAD~1 queried tenantAggregate.getTenantsFromIdentifiers here. Repository-wide git grep for importCustomer calls identifies unchanged callers without a map in importAllCustomersAndUsersInRecords.ts:59, importThreads.ts:140 and importThreadMessage.ts:150. Membership creation at importCustomers.ts:442 only runs when tenantsToLink is nonempty.

findings.title: The NOOP shortcut drops import-job attribution updates
findings.failure: An existing customer with null or different importedByJobDefinitionId returns NOOP when other fields match. CRM imports always supply an empty onUpdate, so they stop updating this stored attribution, omit the customer-changed event, and count the required update as skipped.
findings.fix: Pass importedByJobDefinitionId as the comparison helper's third argument. Cover attribution-only updates from both null and a different job ID in the aggregate litest.
findings.evidence: shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate.ts:16-21 explicitly treats changed attribution as an update. The existing transactional call at customerAggregate.ts:1026-1032 passes it, and lines 1060-1062 persist it. The new call omits it. importCustomers.ts:240 supplies onUpdate: {}, while lines 406-414 forward the job ID. Existing helper tests at shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate.test.ts:105-116 already establish this contract.

findings.title: Propagate failed tenant lookups instead of returning partial success
findings.failure: The helper logs failed chunks, continues, and unconditionally returns Result.ok. Its caller's new isErr branch is therefore unreachable. Once the empty-input bug is corrected, a database or permission failure will masquerade as missing tenants, causing skipped customers or incomplete memberships instead of an import failure.
findings.fix: Return Result.err(lookupResult.error) on the first failed chunk, following the existing Result propagation pattern. Only return a tenant map after all chunks succeed.
findings.evidence: tenantAggregate.getTenantsFromIdentifiers propagates permission and database errors. HEAD~1 importCustomer forwarded those errors through scope.fail. AGENTS.md explicitly requires returning or throwing failed Results rather than logging and continuing. Repository-wide git grep for getTenantsByExternalId and tenantsByExternalId confirms the sole helper/caller pair; the helper has no Result.err return, making lines 514-515 dead.

checked_fine: Deploy: all four changed files are application logic or local tests; no infrastructure, resource identities, exports, deployment ordering, environment variables, secrets or dependency versions change.

Contract: routes, authentication, public schemas and event versions remain unchanged. Email/company updates retain their existing resolution path; customer create/edit permissions still precede the shortcut.
Data: no deletes, retention reductions or migrations are introduced. Tenant membership synchronization remains additive; the findings concern omitted writes.
Silent regression: HEAD~1 already used selectForUpdate: false, so removal of row locking is not a new regression. Genuine NOOPs already omitted customer-change events.
Operability: no deployment-trigger or duplicated configuration changes; successful skips concealing incomplete imports are covered by the findings.
Rollback: HEAD~1 can read the unchanged stored/event schemas; no schema one-way door exists. Completed affected imports require replay as noted above.

Blast radius: the upsert optimization also reaches GraphQL, chat, email, Slack and help-center callers. Creation and actual field changes still follow the transactional path; attribution is the identified comparison mismatch.
Dead code: repository-wide symbol searches found no additional orphaned changed exports or test helpers. The unreachable lookup loop and error guard are covered above.
Design: aggregate boundaries and the shared shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate helper are preserved; the Result propagation departure is reported above.
Validation limit: both changed litests were inspected, but tests and typechecking were not run because node_modules is absent and this review permits neither writes nor network access.
